title: Former Mexican President Vicente Fox and Ex-PAN Governors Defend Ruffo Appel and Allege ‘Political Persecution’
author: Juan Carlos G. Partida
content:
_This article by Juan Carlos G. Partida originally appeared in the[July 24,
2026 edition of La
Jornada](https://www.jornada.com.mx/noticia/2026/07/24/politica/vicente-fox-y-
ex-gobernadores-panistas-defienden-a-ruffo-appel-a-quien-tildan-de-preso-
politico), Mexico’s premier left wing daily newspaper._

**Guadalajara, Jal.,** Former PAN governors and former president Vicente Fox
denounced a **“political persecution”** and called Ernesto Ruffo Appel, also a
PAN former governor of Baja California, a**“political prisoner,”** demanding a
fair trial after he was bound over for trial for the alleged smuggling of
hydrocarbons and organized crime.

At a press conference, the former state leaders of Jalisco, Francisco Ramírez
Acuña and Alberto Cárdenas; former president Vicente Fox; and the former
governors of Guanajuato Juan Carlos Romero Hicks and Miguel Ángel Márquez, who
said they represented 15 former officeholders that emerged from Acción
Nacional, asserted that Ruffo’s arrest “with excessive force” is a form of
“selective and media-driven justice” by the federal government.

**Fox, backed by the other four former governors present, stated that he would
“put his hands in the fire” to vouch for Ruffo** ’s honesty and integrity, and
all of them charged that the man bound over for criminal trial was transferred
to a maximum-security prison, despite his frail health, being over 70 years
old, and the fact that an arrest warrant had previously been denied.
